newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end soft, electricity sector slides.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end soft, electricity sector slides.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed sharply lower with the market led by falls in the heavyweight electricity sector on fears of lower-than-expected second quarter results, said dealers.
The weighted IPSA index closed unofficially down 2.03 percent at 127.34 points. The bolsa was seen falling further at the opening amid renewed earnings speculation.
"We believe that the (electricity firms) will report earnings slightly below expectations and the market is adjusting to that," said Nicolas Allende, a trader at ING Barings.
The general index shed 1.1 percent to 5,603.83 points. Turnover was a moderate 9.8 billion pesos.

Traders noted Chilean stocks were hurt by profit-taking in the wake of the recent rally, coupled with a delayed reaction to the volatility in Brazil which hit other bolsas in the region harder than the Santiago bourse last week.
"There was general profit-taking, not only from local investors but also from abroad. The volume in ADRs was strong as large players are dumping positions," said one dealer.
Chilean-issued American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) closed sharply lower with power investment company Enersis tumbling 8.55 percent to 32-3/4.
Enersis stock shed 5.78 percent to 277 pesos, while Endesa was down 3.59 percent to 295 pesos.
Electricity stocks account for around a 40 percent weighting in the IPSA index.
Winners included pension funs manager Provida, up 2.22 percent at 9,200 pesos and telecom Entel which rose 0.79 percent at 3,190 pesos.
